# Informed compile-time parameter study

Eight complete sources were saved before executing them or editing production
code. This follows the human-authored Issue #33 terminology decision: explicit
compile-time parameter markers use `const`. Existing kind/order/binding/access,
whole-declaration checking and native gates remain. `const` stays contextual
so an ordinary function with that name keeps its meaning. The old `static`
header is a temporary migration control; retiring it remains required work.
General compile-time functions/collections, qfor/body staging keywords,
generic-family notation, QFT, capacities and constitutional admissions are
outside this bounded parameter-header unit. The author had read existing code
and specifications; no independent model or blind benchmark was used. Exact
model identifier/sampling are unavailable. Native check results are not source
preservation proofs. Actual source selection commands and before/after outputs
are recorded separately; no historical command is replayed automatically.

The first observer wrote the wrong manifest key `schema`; all sixteen first calls rejected `project` before grammar checking. Attempt-02 repairs only `schema-version`, retaining identical QLI bytes. Those first failures do not validate parameter grammar.
